parameters.query:
-- §1.13 step 5. The row is written AT cleanup, not before it.
--
-- audio-service deliberately keeps live clip metadata in a sidecar next to the
-- bytes, not in this table (§6.1), so that a row can never outlive the file it
-- describes. That decision leaves `audio_jobs` as the right home for exactly
-- this: the record that survives the clip. A 32-hex object id is a valid UUID
-- without dashes, so it casts directly and the audit trail keys on the same
-- identifier the service used.
--
-- ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE keeps the workflow idempotent: cleaning an already
-- cleaned job refreshes the timestamp rather than raising.
INSERT INTO audio_jobs (id, object_reference, state, cleanup_at)
VALUES ($1::uuid, $2, 'cleaned', now())
ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET
  state      = 'cleaned',
  cleanup_at = now(),
  updated_at = now()
RETURNING id::text, state;

nodes.name: Sweep Expired Clips
nodes.notes: Takes no id, so it cannot be aimed at anything: the deletion set is defined by expiry, not by the caller.

nodes.name: Report Cleanup Failures to WF-000
nodes.notes: A clip that will not delete is a privacy problem, not a cosmetic one -- it is someone's recording staying on disk past its stated lifetime. It goes to the common error handler rather than being logged and forgotten.

assignments.name: payload
assignments.value: ={{ ({ mode: ($json.mode || 'explicit'), object_id: ($json.object_id || null), deleted: ($json.deleted === true), removed: ($json.removed !== undefined ? $json.removed : null), stored_after: ($json.stored_after !== undefined ? $json.stored_after : null), rejected_count: ($json.rejected_count || 0), failed: ($json.has_failure === true), failure_reason: ($json.failure_reason || null) }) }}

nodes.name: Return Cleanup Result
nodes.notes: $json is safe here only because every node that could sit upstream now preserves the item: the Postgres write is followed by Finalize Explicit Result, and the WF-000 call is fire-and-forget. Two separate bugs were caused by assuming that without checking -- a clip reported as not deleted when it had been, and a failure reported as a success.
